Purpose and exclusions

Mounts are a later committed content system only after movement, camera, collision and animation feasibility pass. No mounted sprite, riding pose, mount creature or equipment compatibility is claimed to exist in the archive.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create a feasibility-only mount definition and record all missing sprite/mesh/action requirements. Keep its production Enabled flag false.
  2. Add a test profile to L_TerrainLab with slopes, bridges, doorways and water shores.
  3. Implement movement-profile switching through the existing movement component; no parallel mount teleport integrator.
  4. Create/commission riding/mount art with common root and four/eight-facing plan, then fill appearance matrix and licenses.
  5. Reopen zone/interior/fast-travel rules and UI to show Unavailable until the gate is approved.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
RequestMount(CommandId, MountId) -> Mounted|NotUnlocked|InCombat|ArtUnavailableNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
RequestDismount() -> Dismounted|NoSafePositionNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ValidateMountContent(MountId) -> Feasible|MissingArt|CollisionFailureNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Mount feasibility and later movement/content gate. Rule owner: URPGMountComponent. This asset’s role is Mounts are a later committed content system only after movement, camera, collision and animation feasibility pass. No mounted sprite, riding pose, mount creature or equipment compatibility is claimed to exist in the archive.

  1. Production first proves a developer-authored placeholder mount in the terrain lab, not on a live economy server.
  2. Server validates unlock, zone rules and current action state before changing the movement profile.
  3. Presentation selects a complete mounted set for current facing/action; do not stretch a walking person onto an invented animal.
  4. Dismount finds a valid capsule position and restores the ordinary movement profile once.
  5. Death, transfer, interiors and water use explicit dismount policy; no mount state persists as stale Actor pointers.
  6. Only after art/latency/navigation/camera tests pass may mount entitlements be enabled in catalogs.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_TerrainLab / MountFeasibilityFixture. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
No mounted art -> ArtUnavailable; ordinary movement unaffected.
Dismount inside wall -> NoSafePosition or validated fallback, not clipping.
Mount speed intent forged -> server profile/correction wins.
Transfer while mounted -> documented dismount before snapshot; no duplicate body.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
